source.title: Confess What You Know: Forget-Set Misalignment with Model Knowledge in LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Miso Kim; Georu Lee; Seungwon Jeong; Woojin Lee

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened, but the relevant Table 1 values can be assigned to settings and metrics from the table layout.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how forget-set misalignment affects unlearning and argues that residual knowledge can result from omitted memorized facts, while over-broad requests harm utility. It does not test recovery attacks, so it refines the scope of the broader unlearning claim rather than testing its attack-resistance versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting attacks. Its own GA results measure the direct effects of misaligned forget sets. Table 5 diagnostics and Tables 3–6 comparisons are not recovery-attack outcomes; cited attack and unlearning results are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Most of the study is about forget-set misalignment and its CONFS construction method, which tests no version. However, Appendix C, Table 6 reports RWKU adversarial-attack (AA) probes on the forget set after GA, NPO and RT unlearning of real entities with LLaMA-2-7B-Chat. These probes bear on E (prompt-based recovery) and on A's 'simple attacks don't recover it' part. The Section 3 and Table 1 rows measure omitted-fact leakage and utility damage from misaligned forget sets, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct, but incomplete. The authors also conclude that CONFS, a data-blind confession-based forget-set construction, approaches Gold-standard performance on several metrics. They report it gives a better forgetting–utility balance than other data-blind constructions.
record.recipe_differences: The controlled misalignment analysis uses Gradient Ascent; the broader benchmark experiments compare GA, GD, NPO, and RT with forget sets built by CONFS and other constructions. It does not reproduce the cited recovery-attack methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with forget-set composition: omitting leaked facts leaves them without targeted forgetting, while adding never-seen facts increases retain-set damage.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Unlearning with GA on TOFU: requested leaked facts drop fast (DL+ Prob 0.995→0.312). Omitted leaked facts of the same entity decline only at the retain-set decay rate, and E_eg stays near zero. Adding never-seen facts to the forget set drives most of the retain-set damage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning does not generalize to memorized facts omitted from the forget request, and including non-memorized facts causes collateral utility loss.

record.problems: The controlled misalignment analysis uses synthetic TOFU entities and a limited partition of five QA pairs per subset. Table 1 reports no uncertainty for these values. The study does not evaluate any recovery attack from the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's Real Authors results are omitted because they are general-knowledge utility measures and not needed to record the central omitted-fact and retain-set outcomes. Table 5 misalignment diagnostics and Tables 3–6 method comparisons are not recovery-attack results and are summarized in gate_note.

untested.parts: Accuracy-to-chance on a multiple-choice hazard benchmark. Fine-tuning, quantization and activation attacks.
No activation ablation or block-vs-delete analysis.
Only RWKU's built-in adversarial-attack probe set was used, reported as one aggregate ROUGE-L. No rephrasing, other-language or in-context recovery was tested separately. No per-attack breakdown.
CONFS builds forget sets. It is not proposed or tested as robust against recovery attacks.

missing.what: RWKU forget-set adversarial-attack (AA) probe ROUGE-L after GA, NPO and RT. Pre-trained 0.615. GA 0.104/0.104, NPO 0.147/0.144, RT 0.576/0.502 (RWKU-style/CONFS). Should be compared with the FB and QA probes and with Neighbor/MMLU utility.
RWKU Neighbor-set and utility (MMLU, TruthfulQA, TriviaQA) after unlearning, showing the locality cost alongside forgetting.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T5' with every version marked not_tested was inconsistent. The only version-relevant evidence is RWKU's built-in adversarial probe (Table 6), which the record omitted. For RT, the direct probes barely drop (FB 0.433–0.454 vs 0.475), so attack recovery cannot be judged and no label is given. No uncertainty is reported for Table 6. Table 1 values check against the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning. Its direct performance metrics are not accuracy-to-chance tests.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on an unlearned model.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-access mechanism test.
No recovery test using rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
CONFS constructs forget sets; it is not tested as a counter-method against the listed recovery attacks.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-ascent unlearning with forget set DL+
rows.note: The authors report omitted leaked data degrades at the same rate as the retain set, rather than showing targeted forgetting.
rows.check: Applies to R1–R10. 'Absent' means no targeted forgetting of omitted leaked facts beyond retain-set decay, per the authors (Fig. 2a, Sec. 3.3). Raw DL− values still fall (0.996→0.624 Prob), roughly tracking retain decay. This is a misalignment finding, not a recovery result.

relationships.condition: GA and NPO on RWKU (10 real entities, LLaMA-2-7B-Chat), both forget-set constructions
relationships.reason: From text, not rows (Table 6). Adversarial-attack ROUGE-L stays 0.104–0.147 versus pre-trained 0.615, near the direct FB/QA probe levels. Prompt attacks did not restore the knowledge.
relationships.display_finding: Adversarial-attack ROUGE-L stayed at 0.104–0.147 versus 0.615 pretrained, near direct fill-in-the-blank and question-answering performance.

relationships.reason: From text (Table 6). Forget ROUGE-L falls about 0.5→0.1 on all probes including AA. MMLU and TruthfulQA are maintained (MMLU 0.424–0.433 vs 0.432).
relationships.display_finding: Forget ROUGE-L fell from about 0.5 to 0.1 across all probes, including AA, while TruthfulQA was maintained and MMLU stayed at 0.424–0.433 versus 0.432.

relationships.condition: GA and NPO on RWKU; GA on TOFU
relationships.reason: From text (Tables 3 and 6). On RWKU, Neighbor-set FB drops 0.569→0.34–0.38 and the GA TriviaQA score slips. On TOFU, GA retain Prob falls 0.989→0.33–0.62. General ability is only partly kept.
relationships.display_finding: RWKU neighbor-set FB fell from 0.569 to 0.34–0.38 and GA reduced TriviaQA performance, while TOFU GA retain probability fell from 0.989 to 0.33–0.62.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
